command: import copy,json; import work; req={'claim':'c','conditions':{'recipe':'R','material':'M','regime':'dry'}}; pol={'required_conditions':['recipe','material','regime'],'require_verified':True}; base={'claim':'c','conditions':req['conditions'],'verified':True}; ev=[dict(base,source='old',value={'b':2,'a':1}),dict(base,source='new',value={'a':1,'b':2},supersedes=['old']),dict(base,source='unverified',value=999,verified=False),dict(base,source='withdrawn',value=888,withdrawn=True),{'source':'wrong','claim':'other','value':777,'conditions':req['conditions'],'verified':True}]; before=copy.deepcopy((req,ev,pol)); expected={'status':'supported','value':{'a':1,'b':2},'sources':['new'],'unknowns':[]}; assert work.evaluate(req,ev,pol)==expected; assert (req,ev,pol)==before; assert work.evaluate({'claim':'c','conditions':{'recipe':'R'}},ev,pol)=={'status':'unknown','value':None,'sources':[],'unknowns':['material','regime']}; conflict=[dict(base,source='A',value=1),dict(base,source='B',value=2)]; assert work.evaluate(req,conflict,pol)=={'status':'conflict','value':None,'sources':['A','B'],'unknowns':['source disagreement']}; assert work.evaluate(req,[],pol)=={'status':'unknown','value':None,'sources':[],'unknowns':['no matching evidence']}; false_ev=[dict(base,source='F',value=False)]; assert work.evaluate(req,false_ev,pol)=={'status':'unsupported','value':False,'sources':['F'],'unknowns':[]}; report=json.load(open('report.json',encoding='utf-8')); requests=json.load(open('requests.json',encoding='utf-8')); evidence=json.load(open('evidence.json',encoding='utf-8')); policy=json.load(open('policy.json',encoding='utf-8')); assert report==[work.evaluate(r,evidence,policy) for r in requests]; assert all(set(x)=={'status','value','sources','unknowns'} for x in report); print('all checks passed')

arguments.text: Stage 3 finding: work.py implements pure argument-driven evaluation. It reports sorted missing required conditions before evidence filtering; filters by claim, withdrawal, verification policy, and canonical exact required-condition values; removes superseded eligible source IDs; compares canonical JSON values; preserves Boolean false as unsupported; deep-copies agreed values; and emits exactly status/value/sources/unknowns. report.json matches current requests, evidence, and policy.

Unresolved limits: no known blocker. Implementation assumes valid JSON-shaped inputs and string source IDs, consistent with the supplied schema/data. Canonicalization uses standard json.dumps behavior for supplied JSON values.
